title: Special Array I
statement: Call an array **special** if no two neighbouring values share a parity, so every adjacent pair mixes an even value with an odd one. Return `true` when the integer array `nums` is special and `false` otherwise. A one-element array has no adjacent pairs and therefore counts as special.
notes:
## Intuition

Only neighbouring pairs matter, so one pass over the array is enough. A neat way to test "one even, one odd" is to add the pair: an even plus an odd number is odd, while two evens or two odds always sum to an even number. So the array fails as soon as some adjacent pair has an even sum.

## Approach

1. Walk `i` from 1 to the end, looking at the pair `nums[i - 1]`, `nums[i]`.
2. Compute `pairSum`, their total.
3. If `pairSum` is even, both values share a parity, so return `false`.
4. If no pair failed (including when there is only one value), return `true`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1]`. The loop starts at `i = 1`, which is already past the end, so no pair is checked and the function returns `true`.

For contrast, Example 3 `[4, 3, 1, 6]`: the pair `(4, 3)` sums to 7 (odd, fine), then `(3, 1)` sums to 4, which is even, so the answer is `false`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each adjacent pair is checked once.
- Space: O(1): only the loop index and one sum.

## Pitfalls

- Return `true` only after the loop: returning it inside the loop after the first good pair skips the remaining pairs.
- A single value must return `true`; with no pairs, nothing can break the rule.
- Start the loop at 1 so every step has a left neighbour; starting at 0 reads `nums[-1]`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `i` | index of the right value in the current adjacent pair |
| `pairSum` | `nums[i - 1] + nums[i]`; odd exactly when the parities differ |

narration.1: The function receives the array and answers with a boolean.
narration.2: Visit every adjacent pair; i points at the right-hand value.
narration.3: Add the two neighbours: the sum is odd only when one is even and the other odd.
narration.4: An even sum means both values share a parity.
narration.5: That pair breaks the rule, so the array is not special.
narration.8: Every pair had opposite parity (or there were no pairs), so the array is special.
